title: Café menu labels
context: At a café, let $V=\{\text{falafel wrap},\text{tomato soup},\text{berry bowl}\}$ be the vegan dishes and $G=\{\text{tomato soup},\text{berry bowl},\text{rice pudding}\}$ be the gluten-free dishes.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $V\cap G=\{\text{tomato soup},\text{berry bowl}\}$.**  (true)

Both listed dishes occur in each set, and no other dish does. Thus the claim is **true**.

**B) $\text{rice pudding}\in V\cup G$.**  (true)

Rice pudding is in $G$, so it is in the union. The claim is **true**.

**C) $V\cup G$ contains exactly three dishes.**  (false)

The union is $\{\text{falafel wrap},\text{tomato soup},\text{berry bowl},\text{rice pudding}\}$, which has four dishes. This is **false**.

**D) $V\setminus G=\{\text{falafel wrap}\}$.**  (true)

Only the falafel wrap is vegan but not gluten-free. The claim is **true**.

**E) $V\cap G\subseteq V$.**  (true)

Every item in both sets is certainly in $V$. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The café labels define $V$ and $G$.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$V\cap G=\{\text{tomato soup},\text{berry bowl}\}$, $V\cup G$ has four dishes, and $V\setminus G=\{\text{falafel wrap}\}$.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE: the two shared dishes form the intersection.
**2.** TRUE: rice pudding is in $G$.
**3.** FALSE: the union has four, not three, dishes.
**4.** TRUE: only the wrap is in $V$ alone.
**5.** TRUE: an intersection is a subset of either original set.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

title: Morning weekend shifts
context: Let $M=\{\text{Asha},\text{Ben},\text{Chen},\text{Dina}\}$ be workers assigned a morning shift and $W=\{\text{Ben},\text{Dina},\text{Eli}\}$ be workers assigned a weekend shift.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $M\cap W=\{\text{Ben},\text{Dina}\}$.**  (true)

Ben and Dina are the two names appearing in both lists. The claim is **true**.

**B) $\text{Asha}\in M\cap W$.**  (false)

Asha is in $M$ but absent from $W$; intersection requires both memberships. The claim is **false**.

**C) $|M\cup W|=5$.**  (true)

The distinct workers are Asha, Ben, Chen, Dina, and Eli. The claim is **true**.

**D) $W\setminus M=\{\text{Ben},\text{Dina}\}$.**  (false)

Removing morning workers from $W$ leaves only $\{\text{Eli}\}$. The claim is **false**.

**E) $M\cap W\subseteq W$.**  (true)

Anything in the intersection belongs to $W$ by definition. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
Use the two shift lists.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$M\cap W=\{\text{Ben},\text{Dina}\}$, $M\cup W$ contains five workers, and $W\setminus M=\{\text{Eli}\}$.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** FALSE: Asha is not weekend staff. **3.** TRUE. **4.** FALSE: only Eli is weekend-only. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Warehouse stock lists
context: Let $A=\{\text{K1},\text{K2},\text{K3},\text{K4}\}$ be SKUs in aisle A and $B=\{\text{K3},\text{K4},\text{K5}\}$ be SKUs selected for a promotion.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $A\setminus B=\{\text{K1},\text{K2}\}$.**  (true)

These are the aisle-A SKUs not promoted. The claim is **true**.

**B) $B\setminus A=\{\text{K3},\text{K4}\}$.**  (false)

K3 and K4 are in both sets; $B\setminus A=\{\text{K5}\}$. The claim is **false**.

**C) $A\cap B=\{\text{K3},\text{K4}\}$.**  (true)

These are precisely the shared SKUs. The claim is **true**.

**D) $A\setminus B=B\setminus A$.**  (false)

The two directed differences are $\{\text{K1},\text{K2}\}$ and $\{\text{K5}\}$, so direction matters. The claim is **false**.

**E) $\text{K5}\in B\setminus A$.**  (true)

K5 is promoted but not in aisle A. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The sets record aisle-A and promotional SKUs.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$A\cap B=\{\text{K3},\text{K4}\}$, $A\setminus B=\{\text{K1},\text{K2}\}$, and $B\setminus A=\{\text{K5}\}$.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** FALSE. **3.** TRUE. **4.** FALSE: set difference is directional. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Lab sample screening
context: The universe is $U=\{S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6\}$. Let $P=\{S1,S3,S4\}$ be samples that passed an initial screen.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $P^c=\{S2,S5,S6\}$.**  (true)

The complement contains every universe element not in $P$. The claim is **true**.

**B) $S4\in P^c$.**  (false)

S4 passed, so $S4\in P$, not $P^c$. The claim is **false**.

**C) $P\cup P^c=U$.**  (true)

A set and its complement cover the universe. The claim is **true**.

**D) $P\cap P^c=\{S2\}$.**  (false)

No sample can be both in a set and outside it; the intersection is $\varnothing$. The claim is **false**.

**E) $(P^c)^c=P$.**  (true)

Taking the complement twice returns the original set. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
Complements are taken relative to $U$.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$P^c=\{S2,S5,S6\}$. Also $P\cup P^c=U$, $P\cap P^c=\varnothing$, and $(P^c)^c=P$.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** FALSE. **3.** TRUE. **4.** FALSE. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Camera coverage zones
context: In the set $U$ of all gallery zones, $A$ is the set covered by camera Alpha and $B$ is the set covered by camera Beta.
statements: A zone in $(A\cup B)^c$ is covered by neither camera.
A zone in $A^c\cup B^c$ is covered by neither camera.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $(A\cup B)^c=A^c\cap B^c$.**  (true)

This is De Morgan's law for a union. The claim is **true**.

**B) $(A\cap B)^c=A^c\cap B^c$.**  (false)

The complement of an intersection uses $\cup$, not $\cap$. The claim is **false**.

**C) A zone in $(A\cup B)^c$ is covered by neither camera.**  (true)

Being outside the union means outside both coverages. The claim is **true**.

**D) A zone in $A^c\cup B^c$ is covered by neither camera.**  (false)

This set includes zones missed by at least one camera, including zones covered by the other. The claim is **false**.

**E) $(A\cap B)^c=A^c\cup B^c$.**  (true)

This is the second De Morgan law. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
Camera coverage is modeled by sets $A$ and $B$ in universe $U$.

**Part 1: Key facts.**
De Morgan's laws are $$(A\cup B)^c=A^c\cap B^c$$ and $$(A\cap B)^c=A^c\cup B^c.$$ 

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** FALSE: it uses the wrong connective. **3.** TRUE. **4.** FALSE: the union means missed by at least one. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: T-shirt size and colour choices
context: A shop offers sizes $S=\{\text{small},\text{medium},\text{large}\}$ and colours $C=\{\text{navy},\text{coral}\}$.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $|S\times C|=6$.**  (true)

There are $3\cdot2=6$ ordered choices. The claim is **true**.

**B) $(\text{medium},\text{coral})\in S\times C$.**  (true)

The first coordinate is a size and the second is a colour. The claim is **true**.

**C) $(\text{navy},\text{large})\in S\times C$.**  (false)

The coordinate order is reversed. The claim is **false**.

**D) $S\times C=C\times S$.**  (false)

The counts agree, but their ordered pairs have different coordinate order. The claim is **false**.

**E) $|C\times S|=6$.**  (true)

$|C\times S|=2\cdot3=6$. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The first coordinate of $S\times C$ is a size; the second is a colour.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$|S\times C|=3\cdot2=6$, while $(\text{navy},\text{large})$ has reversed coordinates.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** TRUE. **3.** FALSE. **4.** FALSE. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Newsletter list mismatch
context: Let $P=\{\text{Inez},\text{Jamal},\text{Kara},\text{Luca}\}$ be the print-newsletter list and $E=\{\text{Jamal},\text{Luca},\text{Mei}\}$ be the email-newsletter list.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $P\mathbin{\triangle}E=\{\text{Inez},\text{Kara},\text{Mei}\}$.**  (true)

These subscribers are on exactly one list. The claim is **true**.

**B) $\text{Jamal}\in P\mathbin{\triangle}E$.**  (false)

Jamal is on both lists, which symmetric difference excludes. The claim is **false**.

**C) $P\mathbin{\triangle}E=(P\setminus E)\cup(E\setminus P)$.**  (true)

This is the definition of symmetric difference. The claim is **true**.

**D) $P\cap E\subseteq P\mathbin{\triangle}E$.**  (false)

The intersection and symmetric difference are disjoint. The claim is **false**.

**E) $|P\mathbin{\triangle}E|=3$.**  (true)

The three one-list subscribers are Inez, Kara, and Mei. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
Symmetric difference keeps subscribers on exactly one list.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$P\setminus E=\{\text{Inez},\text{Kara}\}$ and $E\setminus P=\{\text{Mei}\}$, so $P\triangle E$ has three members.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** FALSE. **3.** TRUE. **4.** FALSE. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=FALSE, C=TRUE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Day and night cohorts
context: A training programme has 28 day-cohort students in set $D$ and 22 night-cohort students in set $N$. Each student chooses exactly one cohort.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $D\cap N=\varnothing$.**  (true)

No student can be in both exclusive cohorts. The claim is **true**.

**B) $|D\cup N|=50$.**  (true)

Disjoint sets add: $28+22=50$. The claim is **true**.

**C) $D\setminus N=D\cup N$.**  (true)

Since $D$ and $N$ are disjoint, $D\setminus N=D$, not their union. This statement is therefore **false**.

**D) $D\cap N\subseteq D$ contains 28 students.**  (false)

The intersection is empty and contains zero students. The claim is **false**.

**E) $D\mathbin{\triangle}N=D\cup N$.**  (true)

For disjoint sets, every union member is in exactly one set. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The cohorts are mutually exclusive.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$D\cap N=\varnothing$, $|D\cup N|=28+22=50$, $D\setminus N=D$, and $D\triangle N=D\cup N$.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** TRUE. **3.** FALSE: the difference is $D$. **4.** FALSE. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Helpdesk response criteria
context: In the universe $U$ of helpdesk tickets, $R$ is the set answered within one hour and $S$ is the set receiving a satisfaction rating of at least 4.
statements: A ticket in $(R\cap S)^c$ failed at least one of the two criteria.
A ticket in $R^c\cup S^c$ failed both criteria.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $(R\cap S)^c=R^c\cup S^c$.**  (true)

This is De Morgan's law. The claim is **true**.

**B) A ticket in $(R\cap S)^c$ failed at least one of the two criteria.**  (true)

It is not simultaneously in $R$ and $S$. The claim is **true**.

**C) $(R\cap S)^c=R^c\cap S^c$.**  (false)

The right side means failed both, which is too restrictive. The claim is **false**.

**D) A ticket in $R^c\cup S^c$ failed both criteria.**  (false)

A union means failed at least one criterion. The claim is **false**.

**E) $R\cap S\subseteq R$.**  (true)

Every ticket meeting both criteria meets the response-time criterion. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The ticket conditions are represented by $R$ and $S$.

**Part 1: Key facts.**
$$(R\cap S)^c=R^c\cup S^c.$$ Thus failure of the combined condition means failure of at least one condition.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** TRUE. **3.** FALSE. **4.** FALSE. **5.** TRUE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=FALSE, D=FALSE, E=TRUE

title: Maps and music app users
context: Among 150 commuters, $|M|=92$ use a maps app, $|Q|=67$ use a music app, and $|M\cap Q|=41$ use both.
statements: 51 commuters use only a maps app.
26 commuters use only a music app.
tactical_explanations:
**A) $|M\cup Q|=118$.**  (true)

Inclusion-exclusion gives $92+67-41=118$. The claim is **true**.

**B) 51 commuters use only a maps app.**  (true)

$92-41=51$. The claim is **true**.

**C) 26 commuters use only a music app.**  (true)

$67-41=26$. The claim is **true**.

**D) 32 commuters use neither app.**  (true)

$150-118=32$. The claim is **true**.

**E) $|M\mathbin{\triangle}Q|=77$.**  (false)

The symmetric difference is $51+26=77$, so the claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
The survey gives two overlapping app-user sets.

**Part 1: Formula / Key facts.**
$$|M\cup Q|=|M|+|Q|-|M\cap Q|=92+67-41=118.$$ 

**Part 3: Solve.**
Only maps $=51$, only music $=26$, neither $=150-118=32$, and $|M\triangle Q|=51+26=77$.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE

title: Course enrolment overlap
context: At a college, 84 students take Statistics ($S$), 73 take Programming ($P$), 29 take both, and 140 students were surveyed.
tactical_explanations:
**B) 55 students take Statistics only.**  (true)

$84-29=55$. The claim is **true**.

**C) 44 students take Programming only.**  (true)

$73-29=44$. The claim is **true**.

**D) 12 students take neither course.**  (true)

Since 128 students take at least one course, $140-128=12$ take neither. The claim is **true**.

**E) $|S\cap P|=17$.**  (false)

The overlap is explicitly 29. The claim is **false**.
solution_overview:
Use inclusion-exclusion on the two course sets.

**Part 1: Setup.**
$|S\cup P|=84+73-29=128$, so Statistics-only is 55 and Programming-only is 44. Of the 140 surveyed students, $140-128=12$ take neither course.

**Part 3: Solve.**
**1.** TRUE. **2.** TRUE. **3.** TRUE. **4.** TRUE. **5.** FALSE.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=FALSE

title: Support ticket tags
context: Among 80 support tickets, 38 have tag $U$ (urgent), 31 have tag $B$ (billing), 24 have tag $L$ (login). Also $|U\cap B|=12$, $|U\cap L|=9$, $|B\cap L|=7$, and $|U\cap B\cap L|=4$.
statements: Exactly 4 tickets have all three tags.
Exactly 8 tickets have urgent and billing tags but not the login tag.
The sum $|U\cap B|+|U\cap L|+|B\cap L|$ counts each three-tag ticket three times.
tactical_explanations:
**B) Exactly 4 tickets have all three tags.**  (true)

This is given as $|U\cap B\cap L|=4$. The claim is **true**.

**C) Exactly 8 tickets have urgent and billing tags but not the login tag.**  (true)

Remove the four triple-tag tickets: $12-4=8$. The claim is **true**.

**D) The sum $|U\cap B|+|U\cap L|+|B\cap L|$ counts each three-tag ticket three times.**  (true)

A triple-tag ticket belongs to all three pairwise intersections. The claim is **true**.

**E) 11 tickets have no listed tag.**  (true)

$80-69=11$. The claim is **true**.
solution_overview:
Three tags require three-set inclusion-exclusion.

**Part 1: Formula / Key facts.**
$$|U\cup B\cup L|=|U|+|B|+|L|-|U\cap B|-|U\cap L|-|B\cap L|+|U\cap B\cap L|=69.$$ 

**Part 3: Solve.**
The all-three region is 4; urgent-and-billing only is $12-4=8$; and untagged tickets total $80-69=11$.

**Answer.** A=TRUE, B=TRUE, C=TRUE, D=TRUE, E=TRUE
